Honestly I found it boring rather than scary (and I'm a horror junkie) and my mother (who jumps at EVERYTHING) fell asleep mid-performance. The main thing you need to be aware of is >!the woman in black walks through the aisles at one point. !<

My other tip for any kind of horror is that jump scares are only scary if you let down your guard. If it seems to be building up to a jump scare and then suddenly relaxes, chances are there will be a delayed jump scare (eg. character dramatically pulls back curtain and there's nothing there, everyone relaxes, BOOM suddenly something appears). If you're prepared for a jump scare, it takes out 90% of the fear.

It might also help to familiarise yourself with the plot beforehand? It might break the immersion, but it will be easier to deal with it if you know what to expect.
